A public road may be located, relocated, changed or widened by either of the methods heretofore discussed (Sec. 7841). In proceedings to relocate, change or widen a public road the forms heretofore set out may be modified or adapted to the needs of the particular case without any substantial change. 

Sec. 430. What Are Legally Established County Roads? 

The statute provides that all roads in this State that have been established by any order of the county court, and have been used as public highways for a period of ten years or more, shall be deemed legally established public roads; and all roads that have been used as such by the public for ten years continuously, and upon which there shall have been expended public money or labor for such period, shall be deemed legally established roads; and nonuse by the public for ten years continuously of any public road shall be deemed an abandonment and vacation of the same. (Sec. 7839.)

Thus, the statutory methods of establishing a highway are not exclusive, but the statute recognizes the common law rules that public roads may be established by user, and the right of the public to use highways may be acquired by prescription, and by what is known as common law dedication.66 It has been held that the statute es- 

06 Borchers vs. Brewer, 271 Mo. 137, 196 S. W. 10; School District No. 84 vs. 

Tooloose, (Sup.) 195 S. W. 1023; Brinck vs. Collier, 56 Mo. 160; Borders vs. 

Glenn, (App.) 232 S. W. 1062. 505

COUNTY COURTS 

67 tablishing a road by user has been sufficiently complied with when a road has been used by the public for a period of ten years and a sufficient amount of public money or labor has been expended thereon for such period to keep it in substantial repair or condition for public use even though public money and labor have not been expended each and every year during such period. It has also been held that when a person acquires a right to a roadway by prescription, that right extends only to the land actually used for road purposes and not to other land.68 And, where a prescriptive right was acquired in a road by the public prior to 1887, it has been held that failure to expend money on the road for ten years did not affect the public easement. The fact that a part only of a public road is not used for travel is no evidence of abandonment." The statutory provision authorizing the establishment of a road by user has been held applicable to any public road, whether same was acquired through imperfect proceedings or not," but it does not apply to city streets.72

This statute authorizing proceedings to establish private roads must be strictly complied with.78 The county court has no jurisdiction to proceed to take land for a private road unless it is alleged in the petition that the proposed private road is a way of necessity," and it cannot retain jurisdiction if the petition alleges that the way is one of necessity unless the evidence shows that necessity exists.75 The statute and these rules construing it follow the constitutional provision" and the common law rule that no private property can be taken for private use with or without compensation, unless by the consent of the owner, except for private ways of necessity." Sec. 432. Power to Widen Private Roads. 

and

The county court is authorized to entertain proceedings for the widening of private roads (Sec. 7843). The proceeding may be initiated by the filing of a petition before the county court by an inhabitant of the State or any number of persons who may be interested. The proceeding must be initiated in the county in which the proposed widening is to take effect, and in the petition it must be alleged that the petitioner or petitioners own a tract of land in the county, or in an adjoining county, and that no public road passes through or alongside said tract, and the ingress and egress to and from said tract is over a road heretofore established as a private road, or over a privately owned strip of land. In their petition the applicants may ask for the widening of such road to a width not exceeding forty feet, and establishing of the same as a private road. (Sec. 7843.)

Sec. 433. Proceedings for Establishing or Widening Private Roads. 

It is the duty of the petitioner, at least ten days before the presentation of the petition to establish or widen a private road, to cause a copy of the petition, and a notice of the day on which it will be presented, to be served on the owner or owners of the land through which it is proposed to pass. Such notice may be served on a railroad corporation by serving the agent thereof in the county. If the parties interested are thus notified, the court shall appoint three disinterested commissioners to view the premises and assess the damages to the owner or owners of the land abutting on either side of said private road or strip of land (Sec. 7843). Before proceeding to discharge their duties, the commissioners are required to take and subscribe an oath to honestly, faithfully and impartially discharge their duties under the order of the court. They must then proceed to view the premises and mark out a road, not exceeding forty feet in width, so as to be convenient and to do as little injury as practicable to other persons, and make a report to the county court at its next term, stating the points of beginning and ending, courses, distances and width of said proposed road, and make a report and an assessment of the items of damages sustained by each person through whose land said proposed road passes, including the erection of fences and the kind of fences to be erected, if the land is already enclosed, and, in the opinion of the commissioners, whether the location of the road makes the erection of a fence or fences necessary. (Sec. 7845.) But in such a proceeding a county court is not authorized to bind a petitioner to construct and forever maintain a fence when such fence is required to protect an owner through whose land the road will run. When the commissioners make their report and the proceedings have been regular, and no objections have been made thereto, the county court may order the road established according to the report, and render judgment against the petitioner in favor of each owner of real estate for the amount of damages assessed by the commissioners, whereupon the petitioner shall pay the amount to the county treasurer for the use of the persons entitled thereto, and the necessary costs of the proceedings (Sec. 7846). If the proceedings be found by the court to be irregular, new commissioners may be appointed, with like powers and duties as the former commissioners (Sec. 7847). "Fitzmaurice vs. Turney, 214 Mo. 610, 114 S. W. 504. "Engler vs. Knoblaugh, 131 Mo. A. 481, 110 S. W. 16. 84 509

COUNTY COURTS 

If any person through whose land such road passes shall object on account of the amount of damages awarded to him, an issue shall be made up in the county court, and a new jury sworn to determine the amount of damages to which the objector is entitled, and judgment shall be given in conformity to such findings. The court shall then order the establishment of the road, and the costs of the trial shall be paid by the objector, if the award of the jury shall be the same or less than the award of the commissioners; otherwise the costs shall be paid by the petitioner (Sec. 7848). In the trial before the jury the only question to be submitted to the jury is the amount of damages sustained by the owner of the land as a result of the opening or widening of the road. Its dimensions and course are issues to be determined by the court.85 

At the time judgment is entered establishing the road, the county court shall specify the time when possession shall be given by the owner, and the owner shall be given reasonable time, not exceeding six months, to erect such fences as may be required and to gather his crops, if any, growing on the land (Sec. 7849). If the owner shall neglect or refuse to open the road within the time specified in the judgment, he shall forfeit and pay to the person in whose favor judgment was given five dollars per day as a penalty for each day that it remains unopened, to be recovered in an action of debt before any court having jurisdiction (Sec. 7850).

Sec. 434. Private Roads May Be Made County Roads and May Be 

Vacated.

When a private road has been established, it shall be free to be traveled by persons as a public road, and the county court shall have power, at any time when it considers it of sufficient public utility, to adopt said road as a county road in the same way that it may locate, establish, widen or open new roads (Sec. 7851). The statutes also authorize county courts to vacate private roads by a proceeding requiring the filing of a petition, the giving of notice to interested parties, and an opportunity to file a remonstrance, a hearing and a final order (Secs. 7852-7855).

Sec. 435. Proceedings for Vacating Public Road. 

Proceedings to vacate a public road are similar to those for the establishment, location, relocation and widening of a road. a. Petition for.

The proceeding for vacating a road is initiated by the filing of an application of freeholders of the township or townships through which the road runs. This petition must state that the road sought to be vacated is useless and that the repairing of same is an unreasonable burden upon the district or districts. (Sec. 7836.) 86 The petition must be publicly read on the first day of the term at which it is presented, and the matter continued without further proceedings until the next term of the county court (Sec. 7836). 

86 Witte vs. Sorrell, (Sup.) 219 S. W. 595. 

512

b. Notice and service thereof.

Notice of the filing of such petition and of the road sought to be vacated must be given in two ways. In the first place, notice must be posted up in not less than three public places in the township or townships where the road is located, at least twenty days before the first day of the next term of the county court. In the second place, a copy of the notice shall be personally served on all the persons residing in said district, whose lands are crossed or touched by the road proposed to be vacated, in the same manner as other notices are required to be served by law. (Sec. 7836.) c. Remonstrances, hearing and judgment.

On the first day of the next regular term after the petition is filed and read, and notice given, such petition shall again be publicly read. If no remonstances be made thereto, in writing, signed by at least twelve freeholders, the court may proceed to vacate such road, or any part thereof, at the cost of the petitioners; but if a remonstrance thereto, in writing, signed by at least twelve freeholders, resident of such township or townships, be filed, and the court after considering the same shall decide that it is just to vacate such road, or any part thereof, against the vacation of which the remonstrance was filed, the costs shall be paid by the parties remonstrating, and the original costs and damages for opening such vacated road shall be paid by the petitioners to those who paid the same. But if five years have elapsed since the original opening of the same, no such reimbursement shall be made. (Sec. 7836.) To be effective, remonstrances must be signed by at least twelve freeholders, resident of the township or townships where the road is located.87 The remonstrance must be filed before an order vacating the road is made and same must show that remonstrants are individually affected by the vacation of the road.8 

88 While the statute does not fix the exact time when a remonstrance must be filed, it has been held that if the county court proceeds to hear the petition read on the first day of the next regular term after it is filed and first read, and no remonstrance is then on file, the court may proceed to hear the 

87 In re Big Hollow Road, 111 Mo. 326, 19 S. W. 947. 

88 DeJarnett vs. Tickameyer, (Sup.) 40 S. W. (2d) 686. 513

COUNTY COURTS 

petition and enter an order vacating the road, and a remonstrance filed later on the same day is too late.99 

d. Appeals. 

An appeal lies from an order and judgment vacating a public road. Such appeal may be taken by any party in interest in common as remonstrators, or as an individual affected thereby in any manner, and such appeal may be taken in the same manner as appeals from judgments of the county court establishing a new road. 

The appeal goes to the circuit court, where the case is triable at the first term held within ten days after the taking and filing of the appeal therefrom. (Sec. 7837.) The right of appeal being statutory it cannot be denied," if the appellants have complied with the statute authorizing appeals.1 In order for an interested party to take advantage of the right to appeal, he must file his remonstrance in time and show thereby that he is an interested party. 

92 On an appeal the circuit court proceeds with the trial anew, without regard to the proceeding in the court below. In the hearing of the case in the circuit court, the petitioners have the burden of convincing the circuit court that the road was useless and an unreasonable burden.94 93

B. COUNTY COURTS AND SPECIAL ROAD DISTRICTS 

1. Kinds of Districts.

Sec. 436. Special Road Districts Distinguished. 

A special road district is a political subdivision of the State and of the county in which it exists, formed for the purpose of controlling the building, maintenance and supervision of highways in the territory embraced in such district. Such districts differ from the ordinary common road districts, in that the control of their business is left largely to officers of such special road districts, whereas, com- 515

COUNTY COURTS 

mon road districts are supervised and controlled entirely by county courts and officers appointed by such courts. a. Common road districts.

The county courts of all counties, other than those under township organization, with the advice and assistance of the county highway engineer, are directed to divide their counties into road districts (Sec. 7868) and to appoint road overseers for such districts (Sec. 7870). A road overseer must give bond to be approved by the county court (Sec. 7872), keep the roads in his district in as good repair as the district funds will permit (Sec. 7874), and make detailed reports to the court at each regular term thereof (Sec. 

7875). Such road overseers and the county highway engineer under the supervision of the county court have general charge of the road building within the districts in the counties in the State not under township organization.95 The county court has authority to determine what bridges shall be built and maintained at the expense of the road districts (Sec. 7898), and under the supervision of the county highway engineer may construct and control bridges and order such bridges attached to different road districts for the purpose of keeping same in repair (Secs. 7899-7900).96 b. Nonassessment special road districts. 

In counties not under township organization and St. Louis 

County, such road districts may be formed by vote of the people within the territory embraced in such district, in an election called for that purpose by the county court, upon petition of fifty resident taxpayers of such proposed district (Secs. 8024, 8055). Such special road districts are sometimes referred to as nonassessment special road districts to distinguish them from special road districts organized under the benefit assessment plan. They differ from districts organized under the benefit assessment plan, both in the method of organization and the method by which they are financed. 

95 The statutes governing such road districts, which are ordinarily called "common road districts' to distinguish them from "special road districts,'' are Secs. 7868-7897. 

The power of county courts in connection with the building, maintenance and control of bridges and attaching same to road districts are Secs. 7898-7914, as amended; and Secs. 7915-7970, as amended. 516

c. Benefit assessment districts.

A benefit assessment special road district may be organized by a county court in any county not under township organization (Sec. 

8061) and in any county operating under township organization (Sec. 8176). Such districts are organized upon petition signed by the owners of a majority of the acres of land within a district proposed to be organized (Secs. 8062, 8177). While a benefit assessment special road district is governed largely in the same manner as a nonassessment special road district, the commissioners of the benefit assessment districts are authorized to levy a road tax upon the real and personal property within the district for the purpose of securing funds for road improvement purposes (Sec. 8067), to issue bonds (Sec. 8068), and to apportion and levy special taxes payable in annual installments against the lands in the district according to their proximity to the roads improved, for the purpose of paying the cost of improving roads within the district (Secs. 8069-8073). d. County highways and highway commissions.

For the purpose of unifying and consolidating a State-wide effort to improve roads, the Legislature in 192797 provided for the creation and establishment in each county in the State of a county highway commission composed of four members (Sec. 7856), with power to locate, lay out, designate, construct and maintain, subject to approval of the State Highway Commission, a system of county highways not exceeding in the aggregate one hundred miles in any county, by connecting by the most practical route the several centers of population in the county, in such manner as to afford a connection with such of said centers of population as are not now located on any State highway with such State highways, and so as to afford, as nearly as may be done, a connection with county highways connecting the centers of population of adjoining counties (Sec. 7858). The act gives such commissions absolute jurisdiction and control over all highways constituting a part of the county highway system in their respective counties (Sec. 7862), including highways built through special road districts and in counties under township organization (Sec. 7861). Such commission has the 

Laws, 1927, p. 421. 97 517

COUNTY COURTS 

power to receive and spend in the construction and maintenance of county highways, any money or property that may be appropriated or designated by any municipal corporation, special road district, township, or private individual, and may employ technical and other help to assist in the performance of their duties as prescribed by law (Sec. 7863).

Sec. 437. Nature and Character of Such Road Districts. 

By provisions of the acts authorizing the creation of special road districts, such district are bodies corporate clothed with "the usual powers of a public corporation for public purposes" (Secs. 8025, 8061, 8176). By the acts authorizing their creation, special road districts are political subdivisions of the State for governmental purposes (Secs. 8062, 8177). In dealing with such special road districts, courts have uniformly followed the statutory designation given these districts, and have referred to and treated them as government agencies of a "municipal character, "'98 as municipal corporations exercising governmental functions, as quasi public corporations,100 and as "political subdivisions of the State. Sec. 439. Nature of Power Exercised. 

Proceedings for the incorporation of a special road district have been held to involve the exercise by county courts of legislative power. In the formation of the district, the county court acts as an agency for the Legislature. In delegating to county courts the authority to act for it in this capacity, the Legislature did not violate the rule that a legislative body cannot delegate its authority, for such body has the right to empower certain officers, boards and commissions to carry into effect legislative purposes and enforce legislative regulations." In the formation of such districts, and particularly districts organized under the benefit assessment plan, county courts also exercise judicial power in determining whether the land in the district is to be benefited." But the courts have not 

* State at inf. of Gentry vs. Hughesville Special Road Dist. No. 11 of Pettis 

County, (Sup.) 6 S. W. (2d) 594. 

♦ In State ex rel. Little Prairie Special Road District vs. Thompson, 315 Mo. 

56, 285 S. W. 57 it was said: "Thus the Legislature itself defined and marked out the kind of a territory that may be organized into a road district, and the county court as an administrative agent of the Legislature put the legislative will into effect by ascertaining the facts to be applied in such organization. 

While the proceeding is initiated by persons affected by the organization, the district is created by the Legislature through its appropriate agency." 

The correct rule was stated in Cavanaugh vs. Gerk (Sup.), 280 S. W. 51, as follows: "A legislative body cannot delegate its authority, but alone must exercise its legislative functions It may empower certain officers, boards, and commissions to carry out in detail the legislative purposes and promulgate rules by which to put in force legislative regulations. It may provide a regulation in general terms, and may define certain areas within which certain regulations may be imposed, and it may empower a board or a council to ascertain the facts as to whether an individual or property affected come within the general regulation or within the designated area. 

For a discussion of the same principles, see State on inf. Killam vs. Colbert, 273 Mo. 198, 201 S. W. 52; Merchants' Exchange of St. Louis vs. Knott, 212 Mo. 

616, 111 S. W. 565.

On this point the court in State on inf. of Killam vs. Colbert, 273 Mo. 198, 201 S. W. 52, said: "While authority merely to lay off special taxing districts may be granted by the Legislature to certain boards, or councils, or other administrative bodies, yet before the land included can be burdened with a special assessment for benefits, a notice and opportunity to be heard must be accorded the landowners, in order that the Constitution's 'due process of law' may be satisfied 'Unless the Legislature decide the question of benefits itself, the land- 519

COUNTY COURTS 

always spoken harmoniously on this question. In the formation of nonassessment districts, where the lands included are not thereby subjected to special assessments, judicial power, if exercised at all, is certainly not exercised in the same sense as it is where benefit assessment districts are formed. But it is generally agreed that in the exercise of the power given them, whether it is legislative or judicial, or both, county courts must stay within the statutory regulations prescribed." 

2. Nonassessment Districts. 

Sec. 440. Where Nonassessment Districts May Be Organized. 

The statute provides that territory not exceeding eight miles square, wherein is located any city, town or village containing less owner has the right to be heard upon that question before his property can be taken' (included in the district) ... "From the earliest time it has been held that the act of the county court incorporating a municipal corporation is a judicial act . . In organizing road districts the county court doubtless exercises certain ministerial functions, but necessarily 'judicial questions arise in the course of the proceeding' when the county court passes upon the facts which would give it jurisdiction, when it determines whether or not the petition is properly signed and the notice is duly served. It is a judicial function which the county court must exercise when it determines whether or not the lands included in a district will be benefited by the contemplated improvements.''

Sec. 441. Powers of Nonassessment Districts. 

The statute provides that a special road district of this character shall be a body corporate and possess the usual powers of a corporation for public purposes, and shall be known by some name designated by the county court, in which name such district shall be capable of suing and being sued, and of contracting and being contracted with (Sec. 8025). Such districts are not liable for damages by reason of defects in the road constructed by them.¹2 

Sec. 442. Proceedings for Organization of Nonassessment Dis tricts.

Nonassessment districts are formed by the adoption of the provisions of the statute relative to such district, by majority vote of the qualified voters of such proposed district, voting in an election called for that purpose by the county court (Sec. 8055). a. Petition for.

An election to determine whether or not the applicable sections of the statutes shall be adopted in such proposed district, must be called upon petition therefor being filed by fifty qualified voters who are resident taxpayers of the proposed district. Such petition shall be filed with the county court of the county in which the proposed special road district lies. It shall ask the court to submit the applicable sections of the statutes to a vote of the people of such proposed road district for adoption. (Sec. 8055.)

b. Order calling election.

Upon presentation of such petition to the county court, the court is required to make an order of record that this article, describing the same by its title and date of its approval, be submitted to the voters of such proposed road district at the next general election, or at a special election to be held for that purpose at such time as the court may order (Sec. 8055). c. Notice of election.

When the petition is presented and order made calling such election, notice of such election shall be given by publication thereof in some newspaper published in the county. Such notice shall be published for two consecutive weeks, the last insertion to be within five days next before such election. The court may also give such other notice thereof as it may think proper. The court shall also have ballots printed for such election. On these ballots shall be the words, "For the adoption of the road law" and "Against the adoption of the road law" with the direction, "Erase the clause you do not favor." If the court orders a special election to adopt such provisions of the statute, it must appoint three judges of such election for each voting precinct in such proposed special road district, one of whom shall be the clerk of the election. These judges shall subscribe and take the oath required of the judges of election under the general election law, and shall make their returns of such election to the county court, as judges of election are required to do in general elections. If a majority of the votes cast for and against the adoption of such statute be for its adoption, the court shall declare the result of the vote thereon by an order of record, and make an order of record declaring such article of the statutes to be the law in such special road district, and that the same shall take effect and be in force from and after a day to be named in such order within ten days (Sec. 8055). The corporate existence of the district begins at the time such statutes take effect. 522

Sec. 443. Establishing Government for District. 

Within five days after the adoption of the applicable statutes by the voters of any such road district, the county clerk of the county in which such district is organized shall notify the mayor and members of the city council of any city within such special road district and the judges of the county court of such fact, and call such city councilmen and judges of the county court to meet in the county court room at a specified time within five days from such notice, for the purpose of appointing commissioners for such district (Sec. 

8027). At such meeting the presiding judge of the county court shall preside and the county clerk shall act as clerk. Such meeting must be held within two weeks after the applicable statutes are adopted. (Sec. 8026.) At this meeting the councilmen and judges of the court shall appoint a board of commissioners composed of three persons, all of whom shall be resident taxpayers of the district and shall be chosen to serve until their successors are chosen and qualified. (Sec. 8026.) In the selection of commissioners, the mayor and each councilman of a city in such special road district have one vote for commissioners of such special road district and each of the judges of the county court has one vote.18 If the city is located a greater distance than ten miles from the meeting place of the county court, the mayor and city council of the city or town within the road district for which commissioners are to be appointed may make a written certificate of their choice of the commissioner or commissioners to be appointed, designating their first, second and third choice, and seal the same and transmit it to the county clerk by mail or by special messenger, and selection designated in such certificate shall be given the same consideration as though the board and mayor were present at the meeting of the court. Such certificate shall be given over the signature of the mayor or acting mayor, and it must be attested by the seal of the city and signature of the city clerk. (Sec. 8026.) The clerk of the county court shall notify each commissioner of his appointment within five days from such appointment (Sec. 8028). Sec. 444. Powers and Duties of Commissioners. 

Subject to such supervision and control as the county court exercises over it, the board of commissioners has general charge of the roads of the district. Upon the organization of the board of commissioners of such special road district, the county court shall deliver to the board all the tools and machinery used for working roads belonging to the districts formerly existing within the territory embraced in such special district, taking a receipt from the board for the same, and such board shall keep and use such tools and machinery for constructing and improving public roads (Sec. 

8032). The statute provides that the board shall have sole, exclusive and entire control and jurisdiction over all public highways within its district, outside the corporate limits of any city or village therein, to construct, improve and repair such highways, and shall remove all obstructions from such highways, and for the discharge of these duties shall have all the power, rights and authority conferred by general statutes upon road overseers, and said board shall at all times keep the public roads under its charge in as good repair as the means at its command will permit, and for this purpose may employ hands at fixed compensations, rent, lease or buy teams, implements, tools and machinery, all kinds of motor power, and all things needful to carry on such road work. It may have any of 

524

such work done under contract, under such regulations as the board may prescribe. (Sec. 8033). It has been held that, under such statutory power, the board of commissioners of a special road district has the right to determine what roads in the district shall be improved and the manner in which the improvement shall be made, and that a court of equity will not enjoin the board from doing what the law has declared it shall do.¹ The statute gives such board authority to expend not more than one-fourth of the revenue which may now or which may hereafter be paid into its treasury for the purpose of grading and repairing any roads or streets within the corporate limits of any city within such special road district, and for the purpose of constructing and maintaining macadam, gravel, rock or paved roads or streets within the corporate limits of any city within such district, but such board is prohibited from expending any of its revenue outside of the county in which such special road district is situated (Sec. 8034). It may repair, grade, gravel, macadamize, pave or otherwise improve, to the distance of fifteen miles from any line of such special road district, any highway outside of such district, if the same be a prolongation of an improved street or highway in said district and if liberal contributions toward such improvements be made in money, material or labor by the inhabitants interested in such improvements, or the county court or any special road district in the State, or the State Highway Board, or the United States Government, or by any one or more thereof (Sec. 8036). It has the right to sell any property of such district, on such terms as it may deem proper, when same can no longer be profitably used for road work (Sec. 8037). It may buy all material which may be used, directly or indirectly in constructing, improving or repairing any public highway or bridge in its district, and is authorized to do and perform all acts within its district for which any authority is given to road overseers under the general road law of this State (Sec. 8039). It may build, repair and maintain or cause to be built, repaired or maintained all bridges and culverts needed within the district (Sec. 8039).15 "Schmidt vs. Berghaus, 205 Mo. A. 409, 223 S. Sec. 445. Funds of District.

Funds for any public road districts thus organized are derived from county taxes for road purposes, and from money collected for pool or billiard table licenses, upon business within the district; it being the duty of the county court, as such taxes and licenses are paid and collected, to apportion and set aside to the credit of such special road district from which such taxes were collected, all taxes arising from and collected and paid upon any property lying and being within such special road district, and one-half of the amount collected for pool and billiard table licenses so collected from such business carried on within the limits of such district. The commissioners of such district shall make written application for such funds to the county court, and thereupon the county court shall draw warrants upon the county treasurer for the funds available for said district. (Sec. 8042.) But mandamus will not lie, at the instance of special road district commissioners, to compel judges of the county court to pay to the district money collected where such money has been expended for debts contracted before the organization of the district, and there is no fund upon which a writ of mandamus could operate.16 But mandamus will lie to compel the 

16 State ex rel. Wainwright-Steedman Special Road District of Callaway 

County vs. Holman, 305 Mo. 195, 264 S. W. 908. 526

judges of a county court to remit funds derived from taxes collected from property in the district to the commissioners of such district.¹7 

Where no application is made by the board of commissioners to the county court for several years for the district's proportionate part of such taxes, it was held that the district was not entitled to recover the proportion of taxes for such years expended on roads in other districts where there were no special road district debts outstanding for those years. 18 Funds for these districts are also derived from a poll-tax on all able-bodied male inhabitants of the district, between the ages of twenty-one and sixty years (Sec. 8043), to be collected through the cooperation of the commissioners of the road district and the county clerk (Secs. 8043-8046). The funds derived from such sources shall constitute a general district road fund and shall be used for working, repairing and improving the public roads of the district, and for no other purpose. No part of such fund shall be used for paying damages and costs for opening new roads paid by the county out of the county revenue, unless otherwise provided (Sec. 8047). Such board shall not become indebted in any manner or for any purpose to an amount exceeding in any one year the income and revenue provided for such year, except for bonded indebtedness (Sec. 8053).

Sec. 446. Supervision of District by County Court. 

In addition to the authority given by law to county courts to supervise the establishment of such special road districts and organize the government thereof, the county courts and any city council of any city in the district exercise additional supervisory control of such districts. The board of commissioners is required to make annual settlements with the county court in the August term thereof. These settlements must contain a full and itemized 

17 State ex rel. Monett Special Road District vs. Barry County, 302 Mo. 279, 258 S. W. 710; State ex rel. Moberly Special Road District of Randolph County vs. Burton, 283 Mo. 41, 222 S. W. 844. 

18 Little Prairie Special Road District vs. Pemiscott County, 297 Mo. 568, 249 

S. W. 599. 527

COUNTY COURTS 

statement of all moneys received and from what sources and for what purpose the same have been expended. They must be subscribed and sworn to by at least two of the members of the board and a copy of same must be filed with the city clerk and may be published in the discretion of the city council (Sec. 8043). Proceedings for the extension of the boundaries of the district must be carried on in the county court in the manner prescribed by the statute (Sec. 8059). Outside of these supervisory or regulatory powers exercised by county courts over special road districts the responsibility for the operation and management of the business of the districts, which rested on the courts themselves under the common district plan, has been shifted to the board of commissioners by the special road district laws. 

Sec. 447. Dissolution. 

Any such district may be abandoned or dissolved in the same manner in which it is created, at any time after it has been in existence for a period of four years (Sec. 8057). Such abandonment or dissolution may be accomplished by resubmitting the proposition as to whether or not the applicable sections of the statute shall be adopted, upon the petition of fifty resident taxpayers of the district. 

If the majority of the votes of the district be cast against it, the operation of the law shall cease in said district. (Sec. 8057.)

Sec. 448. Payment of Bonds After Dissolution. 

The statute provides that when any special road district may be disorganized, disincorporated or abolished, owing at the time any outstanding bonds, the state auditor of the State of Missouri shall certify to the county court in which such district is located, the necessary amount of money that will be required to pay the principal and interest on the bonds of such district coming due and maturing in the next succeeding year. It then becomes the duty of the county court, upon receipt of such certificate, to determine and levy a rate of taxation which will produce the amount of money required for the next succeeding year to pay off the amount of the principal and interest on such bonds for that year. (Sec. 8058.) 528

3. Benefit Assessment Special Road Districts. 

Sec. 449. County Courts May Form Benefit Assessment Districts. 

The statute authorizes county courts of counties not under township organization to divide the territory of their respective counties into road districts (Sec. 8061). Such districts may be of any di mensions that may be deemed necessary or advisable, except that every district shall be included wholly within the county organizing it and shall contain at least six hundred and forty acres of contiguous territory. But the county courts are prohibited from dividing the territory within the corporate limits of a city having a population of 150,000 into such road district. Any district thus formed is given the usual powers of a public corporation for public purposes, and has the right to sue and may be sued, may contract and be contracted with, and may own such real estate and personal property as may be donated to it or purchased by it in accordance with the law. (Sec. 8061.) 532

Sec. 450. Proceedings for Organization of Assessment Districts. 

a. Petition for.

A petition for the organization of a benefit assessment special road district must be signed by the owners of a majority of the acres of land within the territory proposed to be organized into a district. 

It must set forth the proposed name of the district, and give the boundaries thereof and the number of acres owned by each signer of such petition, and the whole number of acres embraced in the entire district, the names of other owners of land within the proposed district, so far as the same are known, the number of acres owned by each, so far as known, and contain a prayer for the organization of a public road district in accordance with the article applicable to such districts. Such petition must be filed in the office of the county clerk thirty days before the beginning of the next regular term of such court. (Sec. 8062.) 

b. Notice. 

The clerk of the county court is required to give notice of the filing of such petition by at least three publications in some weekly newspaper printed in the county, and by at least five handbills put up at public places within the district, which notice shall show the date of the beginning of the next regular term of the county court at which same may be heard, must contain the names of at least three signers of said petition, set out the boundaries of the proposed district, and must notify all owners of land in the proposed district who may desire to oppose the formation thereof to appear on the first day of such regular term of court and file their written remonstrance thereto (Sec. 8062). The filing of a proper petition and the giving of notice as is required by the statute are jurisdictional, and the county court is not authorized to order the incorporation of a district containing territory described differently from that described in the petition, where there is no remonstrance and no amended petition filed.19 A clerical error in the published notice, however, has been held not to invalidate the organization of the district.20 "State on inf. of Killam vs. Colbert, 273 Mo. 198, 201 S. W. 52. 

20 State at inf. of Gentry vs. Hughesville Special Road District No. 11 of Pet tis County, 6 S. W. (2d) 594, 319 Mo. 1246. 533

COUNTY COURTS c. Remonstrance. 

Any landowner owning land within the district may file a separate remonstrance against the formation of the proposed district, or all such owners may join in one remonstrance. Each remonstrance must be in writing and must state specifically and separately the objection or objections of the remonstrators to the formation of such proposed road district. Every remonstrance must be filed with the clerk of the county court where the proceedings are pending, on or before the first day of the next regular term of court after the petition is filed. (Sec. 8062.) d. Hearing and determination.

On the first day of the next term of the court after such petition is filed, or as soon thereafter as its business will permit, the county court shall hear such petition and remonstrance, and shall make any change in the boundaries of such proposed district as the public good may require and make necessary, and if, after such changes are made, it shall appear to the court that such petition is signed or in writing consented to by the owners of a majority of all the acres of land within the district as so changed, the court shall make an order incorporating such public road district, and such order shall set out the boundaries of such district as established. If no remonstrances shall have been filed, or all remonstrances filed are overruled by the court, the court shall determine whether such petition has been signed by the owners of a majority of the acres of land in the district, and, if so, shall make an order incorporating the district with the boundaries given in the petition, or with such boundaries as may be set forth in an amended petition signed by the owners of a majority of the acres of the land affected thereby. Such amended petition may be filed at any time before the making of the order establishing a road district, but the boundaries proposed for the district shall not be so changed as to embrace any land not included in the notice given by the clerk, unless the owner thereof shall in writing consent thereto, or shall appear at the hearing, and be notified in open court of such fact and given an opportunity to file or join in a remonstrance. The statute provides that when an order is made incorporating a district in this manner, such district 534

shall become a political subdivision of the State for governmental purposes. (Sec. 8062.) It has been held that if the county court errs in calculation or in excluding names from petitions for such special road district, its action is not reviewable by quo warranto, for the reason that same is judicial.21

Sec. 451. Establishing Government for District. 

At the term of court when an order is made establishing such district, or at a subsequent term, the court shall appoint three commissioners, who shall be residents of the district, who shall hold their office until the first Tuesday after the first Monday in January thereafter. On said date, the voters of the district, at an hour and place to be fixed by said commissioners, shall elect three commissioners, one of whom shall serve for one year, one for two years and one for three years. Such commissioners elected must be resident landowners of the district. After their selection, commissioners must qualify by taking an oath that they will faithfully, honestly and impartially discharge their duties according to law. If such commissioners fail to call an election, the county court may call same. (Sec. 8063.)

Sec. 452. Powers of Commissioners. 

After the commissioners are appointed and qualified, they are required to meet at a time and place within such district as may be fixed by the county court at the time of appointing them, or as they may in writing agree upon. They shall organize by electing one of their number president, another vice-president and another secretary. But by unanimous vote of all the commissioners any person not a member of the board may be chosen secretary. After the organization meeting, the commissioners shall meet at such time and place as they may agree upon in writing, or the president or vice-president may order. The county treasurer is made the treasurer of the board. (Sec. 8064.) When the board is organized, the county court shall cause all tools and machinery used for working roads, belonging to the districts formerly existing and composed of 

State at inf. Mayfield ex rel. Cook vs. Dougan, 305 Mo. 383, 264 S. W. 997. 535

COUNTY COURTS 

territory embraced within the incorporated district, to be delivered to said commissioners, for which such commissioners shall give a receipt, and such commissioners shall keep and use such tools and machinery for constructing and improving public roads and bridges. 

The statute gives such commissioners sole, exclusive and entire control and jurisdiction over all public highways, bridges and culverts within the district, and power to construct, improve and repair such highways, bridges and culverts. Commissioners have the same rights and authority conferred by law upon road overseers, and are charged with the responsibility of keeping the roads, bridges and culverts in the district in as good condition as the means at their command will permit. (Sec. 8065.) The commissioners also have power to levy for the construction and maintenance of bridges and culverts in the district, and working, repairing and dragging roads therein, general taxes on property taxable in the district and power and authority to levy special taxes for the purpose of paying interest on bonds when it falls due, and to create a sinking fund sufficient to pay the principal of such bonds at maturity (Sec. 8067). The commissioners have further authority to propose the issuance of bonds and order an election to be held in the district for the purpose of determining whether or not such bonds shall be issued (Sec. 

8068). The commissioners are empowered to proceed in the improvement of roads in the district when there is filed before them a petition signed by the owners of a majority of the acres of the land in the district that is within one-half mile of a public road or a part of a public road (Sec. 8069). In such proceedings, landowners are given the right to protest, object and except to the improvement of such road, and, after a hearing before the county court, the improvement may be made and paid for by special assessments against the land in the district (Secs. 8070-8075). It has been held that the law providing for the State highway system, did not repeal the law for the organization of special road districts,22 and that a county court did not lose jurisdiction over a proceeding to organize a special road district by reason of an order of dissolution which was subsequently quashed on certiorari (Sec. 8074). It has further been held "Johnson vs. Underwood, 24 S. W. (2d) 133, 324 Mo. 578. 536

that the statute contemplates a special road improvement and that the law does not permit the making of changes.2 

Sec. 453. 

Dissolution of District. 

Such special road districts may be dissolved upon the verified petition of any owner of land in the district, stating that such district has no commissioners and has failed to elect commissioners at any regular election, or has failed to hold a special election to fill any vacancy in the office of commissioner, or that such road district has ceased to perform the functions for which it was created. After such petition is filed, notice is given and if no one in interest shall appear and show that the district is performing the functions for which it was created, and that good cause exists why the district should not be dissolved, the county court shall enter an order that the district be dissolved. (Sec. 8081.) Or such district may be dissolved when a petition, signed by the owners of a majority of the acres of land within the district, shall be filed with the county court of any county where the district is located, setting forth the name of the district and the number of acres owned by each signer of the petition and the whole number of acres of the district (Sec. 8082). 

If such petition is filed, notice thereof must be published for three weeks successively in some newspaper in the county, prior to the hearing of the petition. 

Sec. 454. Obligations of District Upon Dissolution. 

The dissolution of such district shall not relieve the district of the necessity of paying the bonds issued against the same, nor affect the validity thereof or the collection of taxes that may have been levied or assessed against lands within the district (Sec. 8081). Nor shall such dissolution invalidate or affect any contract entered into or imposed on such road district (Sec. 8083). 

Sec. 455. Trustee Appointed for Disincorporated District.

Whenever the county court shall dissolve any such road district, 

"Platte City Benefit Assessment Special Road District vs. Couch (Sup.), 8 

8. W. (2d) 1003. 537

COUNTY COURTS 

such court shall appoint some competent person to act as trustee for the district, who must qualify and give bond for the faithful discharge of his duties (Sec. 8084). This trustee shall have power to prosecute and defend to final judgment all suits instituted by or against the district, collect all moneys due the same, liquidate all lawful demands against the same, and for that purpose shall sell any property belonging to such road district, or so much thereof as may be necessary, and generally to do all acts requisite to bring to a speedy close all the affairs of the road district. For that purpose, such trustee, under the order and direction of the county court, shall have the right to exercise all the powers given by law to the district. (Sec. 8085.) When the trustee shall have closed the affairs of the road district, and shall have paid all its debts, he shall pay over to the county treasurer all the money remaining in his hands and deliver to the clerk all books, papers, records and deeds belonging to the dissolved road district (Sec. 8086).

COUNTY COURTS C. COUNTY COURTS AND DRAINAGE DISTRICTS Sec. 456. Methods for Drainage of Swamp Lands. 

Swamp or overflowed lands may be drained through cooperative enterprises of the owners of such lands organized for such purpose into drainage districts under the circuit court drainage district act (Secs. 10743-10808), or under the county court drainage district act (Secs. 10809-10864), or the drainage of such lands may be carried on through proceedings which do not require the formation of drainage districts (Secs. 10865-10877). The proceedings for the drainage of lands under the county court drainage district act and under the act authorizing drainage without the organization of drainage districts are carried on before the county court. The formation of drainage districts in county courts for the purpose of draining swamp or overflowed lands being the most frequently used of the latter two methods, particular attention will be given to such proceedings.

Sec. 457. Power of County Court to Form Drainage Districts. 

The statute authorizes the county court of any county in this State to organize, incorporate and establish drainage districts, and to cause to be constructed, straightened, widened, altered or deepened any ditch, drain, natural stream—not navigable, bank protection, current control, or watercourse, when the same is necessary to drain or protect any land or other property, and when it shall be conducive to the public health, convenience or public welfare, or when it will be of public utility or benefit (Sec. 10809). It has been held that where such a statute is intended to subserve a great public purpose conducive to the public health, convenience and welfare, it should not be confined by technical construction within an extremely narrow compass, but should be construed so as to be in harmony with the legislative intent and to facilitate its accomplishment.25 That statutory authority for the construction of drainage districts by county courts includes not only the right to drain the 

25 State ex rel. Marshall vs. Bugg, 224 Mo. 537, 123 S. W. 827. 544

land, but also to protect the banks or control the current of streams and even install current retards in a navigable river.26 

Sec. 458. Petition and Bond for Drainage District. 

Before any county court may organize, incorporate and establish a drainage district, or make any improvement authorized by law to be made by such district, there must be filed with the clerk of the county court a petition signed by one or more landowners whose lands will be liable to be affected by or assessed for the construction of the improvements necessary to be made. This petition must set forth: (a) The necessity for the proposed improvement, as well as the starting point, route and terminus thereof; (b) the boundary of the proposed district; (c) the names of the owners of lands or other property within the boundary of such proposed district, together with a description of the said lands or other property owned by each. If the owner of such land is unknown, that fact shall be stated. There shall be filed with such petition, a bond in the sum of not less than fifty dollars per mile, payable to the State of Missouri, signed by one or more of the petitioners, with two or more good and sufficient freehold sureties. If a landowner signs a petition for the formation of a drainage district in the county court, he cannot have his name stricken from the petition without the written consent of the owners of a majority of the acreage represented by those signing the petition. (Sec. 10810.) 

Sec. 459. Appointment of Attorneys, Viewers and Engineer.

At the first term of the court after the filing of the petition the statute requires that the court appoint one or more attorneys, satisfactory to the owners of a majority of the acreage represented by those signing the petition, to assist in the establishment of the district and advise with its officers, agents and employees, and prepare reports and other necessary documents. The compensation of such attorney shall be just and shall be taxed as costs in the case. (Sec. 

10811.) Immediately after the petition and bond have been filed 

*State ex rel. Harmony Drainage Dist. No. 3 of Saline County vs. Hackmann, 

305 Mo. 685, 267 S. W. 608. 545

COUNTY COURTS 

and the bond approved, the court shall without delay appoint a competent civil and drainage engineer, and three persons as viewers, who shall be freeholders residing within the State of Missouri, and not landowners in the proposed district nor of kin within the fourth degree of consanguinity to any person owning land within the boundary line set forth in the petition. The court shall enter an order, certified by the clerk, for such viewers and engineer to view the location of the proposed ditch or improvement and the premises along and adjacent thereto. 

Sec. 460. Proceedings and Report of Viewers and Engineer. 

A majority of such viewers constitutes a quorum and controls in all matters. These viewers and engineer are required to take oath to discharge their duties faithfully and to make a true report of the work done and the facts by them ascertained. They shall view the location of the proposed ditch or improvement and the premises along and adjacent thereto. If they find that the proposed improvement is necessary, practicable and would be of public utility or conducive to the public health, convenience or welfare, they shall so report and in their report they shall indicate approximately the proper character, dimension, location and probable cost of the improvement necessary to accomplish the object of the petition, and, if necessary to determine the facts, the engineer may employ assistants and make surveys, and with the approval of the court he may employ a consulting engineer or secure expert advice. They shall also ascertain and report what land or other property, if any, adjacent to the proposed drainage district will be benefited by the improvement, and shall prepare and submit as a part of their report a description of such lands or other property, with the names of the owners thereof when the same can be ascertained by reasonable diligence, and shall also set forth the boundary line of said proposed district so as to include the additional land or other property. They shall report their findings in writing with such maps, profiles and drawings as are necessary to advise the court in the premises and shall promptly file the same with the county clerk. (Sec. 10812.)

It has been held that where a report by the viewers showed that 546

they made "a thorough examination" of the proposed system from end to end, and such report was accompanied by a plat which showed "the line examined by" them, there was a sufficient compliance with the requirement that they view the premises.27 It is the duty of the viewers to apportion to public or corporate property the same proportionate costs of construction in proportion to the benefits as to private individuals.28

Sec. 461. Publication of Notice of Hearing. 

Immediately after the report of viewers and engineer has been filed, the county clerk must cause notice thereof to be published in some newspaper published in the county wherein the proceedings are pending. Such notice shall be published once a week for three consecutive weeks (3 times). (Sec. 10813.) If the notice is to all named persons and to all other persons owning land described, it is sufficient.29 The statute does not require that the notice give the names of the owners of the land in the proposed district, and it has been held that if the notice invited the persons concerned to attend the hearing, it is sufficient.80 And a notice which follows the statutory form, but omits the article of the statutes under which the proceeding is being held, has been held sufficient.31 Since the purpose of such notice is to inform the persons interested of the proposed scheme of drainage so that they may appear for the purpose of consulting among themselves and with the county court regarding the advisability of the proposed scheme, notice is sufficient which substantially complies with the form prescribed by statute.32 Notice must be given by the clerk instead of by the court, and it need not include the place of beginning, route and terminus (Sec. 10813).88 "State ex rel. COUNTY COURTS Sec. 462. Remonstrances. 

Not later than ten days after the last day of publication of said notice, any person interested in land or other property that will be affected by the organization of the proposed drainage district, or by the proposed improvement, may file in the office of the county clerk a written remonstrance against or objection to the petition or report of the viewers, setting forth therein his grievance against the proposal (Sec. 10814).

Sec. 463. Hearing of Petition and Remonstrances. 

The court may then hear and determine all such remonstrances and objections in a summary manner. The court shall then consider the petition and determine and enter an order recording its findings as to whether the owners of a majority in acreage of the proposed district are petitioners or have joined in the prayer of said petition. The court shall, if it finds that the owners of a majority in acreage of the proposed district are petitioners, or if less than such majority are petitioners, it may, in its discretion, find in favor of making the improvement. If the court finds in favor of making the improvement the petitioners shall be immediately released from their liability and bond. If the court finds in favor of making the improvement, it shall, by order of record, incorporate the land and other property described in the report of the viewers and engineer, or any part thereof, into a drainage district, which it shall designate by number. If the court finds against the improvement, it shall dismiss the proceedings at the cost of the petitioners. (Sec. 10814.)

Sec. 464. Legal Status of District. 

The statute provides that when the county court orders that a drainage district be established, such district shall be a body corporate and a political subdivision of the State, and that such district shall possess the usual powers of a corporation for public purposes, shall be capable of suing and being sued in its corporate name, and shall be capable of holding such real and personal property as may be at any time either donated to or acquired by it in accordance with the law (Sec. 10814). And the legality of an order incorpor- 548

ating such district cannot be inquired into collaterally, such as in a suit by the district to collect assessments.84 

Sec. 465. Court Shall Levy Tax to Pay Preliminary Expense. 

When any such district has been incorporated and established, the court shall, by order entered of record, levy a uniform tax of not more than fifty cents per acre upon each acre of land and other property within the district, to be used for the purpose of paying expenses incurred or to be incurred in organizing said district, making surveys of the same and assessing benefits and damages and paying the other expenses necessary to be incurred before said court shall be empowered to levy taxes or to issue bonds and thereby provide funds to pay the total cost of the improvements of the district. Any excess of funds derived from such tax over the amount of the preliminary expense shall be paid into the fund for the construction of the improvement. (Sec. 10815.)

Sec. 466. Court Shall Appoint Viewers Who Shall Permanently Locate District and Assess Benefits and Damages. 

Immediately after a district is established, the court shall, by an order of record, direct the viewers and engineer theretofore appointed, or appoint others possessing the same qualifications, and they shall proceed to view the lands and other property in the district and establish the precise location where, in their judgment, the proposed improvement will prove most efficient, and shall determine the dimensions and form of the proposed ditch, levee or other improvement. They may, if deemed best, vary from the lines of the ditches described in the petition, provided they follow the line as nearly as practicable. If necessary to obtain sufficient fall or outlet, they may extend the outlet below the point named in the petition.

Sec. 467. Publication of Notice of Filing of Viewers' Report. 

Upon the filing of the report of the viewers and engineer, the clerk of the county court is required to give notice of the filing thereof, by publication in some newspaper published in the county wherein the proceeding is pending. Such notice shall be published for three successive weeks (three times) and shall be substantially in the form prescribed by the statute. (Sec. 10819.) The drainage act has been held to be a code unto itself in respect to the manner of organization of drainage districts and the condemnation of lands by such districts and a review of the proceedings under the act, and all the proceedings under that act are in rem.36 Where a notice of the filing of the viewers' report sets out the names of twenty alleged landowners and continues with "to all other persons who may own such land hereinafter described or any part thereof," and plaintiff's husband was among the twenty named owners, the notice was held sufficient to give the county court jurisdiction over the person of the plaintiff. Sec. 469. Hearing and Order. 

All exceptions to the viewers' report are heard by the court and determined in a summary manner so as to carry out liberally the purposes and needs of the district. If it appears to the satisfaction of the court, after having heard and determined all of said exceptions, that the estimated cost of constructing the proposed improvement is less than the benefits assessed against the land and other property in the district, then the court shall approve and confirm the viewers' report as modified and amended. The court shall adjudge and apportion the costs incurred by the exceptions filed and shall condemn any land, within or without the boundary lines of the district, that is shown by the report of the viewers to be needed for rights of way, holding basins and other works, or that may be needed for material to be used in constructing said works, follow- ...

The names to be inserted in the aforesaid notice are usually obtained by the viewers while inspecting and locating the right of way for the ditch, and such notice should, in addition to the names returned by the viewers, also designate generally all other persons whose lands will be affected by the proposed improvements. Such notice, when duly published, is due process of law." "State ex rel. Kersey vs. Sims (App.), 286 S. W. 832. 552

Sec. 470. Appeals. 

The statute provides that any person may appeal to the circuit court from the judgment of the county court, and upon such appeal there may be determined either or both of the following questions: 

First, whether just compensation has been allowed for property appropriated, and second, whether proper damages have been allowed for property prejudicially affected by the improvements. 

Appeals shall be granted in these cases where the appellant shall, before the end of the term of the county court and within ten days from the date of the order appealed from, file a written application for an appeal, specifying therein the matters appealed from, verified by affidavit as in appeals taken from judgments of circuit courts, and the application shall be recorded upon the record of the county court. The county court shall then fix the amount of the bond to be given by the appellant and cause an entry thereof to be made upon its record. And appellants shall, within ten days thereafter, file with the clerk a bond payable to the drainage district in the amount fixed by the county court, with at least two good and sufficient freehold sureties, to be approved by the court, or in vacation by the clerk, conditioned to pay all costs on the appeal in case the appellant fail to sustain the same, or the appeal be for any reason dismissed. Within ten days from the date of filing said bond, the clerk shall make and certify a transcript of the proceedings had before the county court relating to the land of appellant and involved in the appeal, and file the same, together with all original papers relating to the proceedings, on file in his office, in the office of the circuit court, but proceedings in the county court shall not be stayed by such appeal, or prevent progress in the work of constructing any work or improvement, but the county court may pro- "State ex rel. Kersey vs. Sims (App.), 286 S. W. 832. 553

Sec. 471. Report May Be Amended by Viewers. 

After hearing the exceptions to the report, the court may, if it deems advisable, refer the report back to the viewers, with or without directions for correction or amendment in any particular, in which event a new notice shall be given in conformity with the form therefor prescribed by statute. Exceptions to an amended report may be filed in like time and manner as the original report, and proceedings thereafter shall be the same as in the case of the report of the first instance. (Sec. 10820.)

Sec. 472. Additional Authority to Condemn. 

The statute authorizes the county court to condemn for the use of such district any necessary land or other property not acquired or condemned on the report of the viewers, following also the procedure for condemning land for telegraph, telephone and railroad rights-of-way (Sec. 10822).

Sec. 473. County Court May Levy Tax for Benefits Assessed. 

The statute provides that immediately after the approval and confirmation of the report of the viewers, the court shall, by order "Western Tie & Timber Co. vs. Naylor Drainage Dist. Such tax shall be apportioned to and levied on each tract of land in said district in proportion to the benefits assessed and not in excess thereof. Where bonds are issued, then the amount of the interest (as estimated by the court) which will accrue on such bonds shall be included and added to the tax. The court may, by its order, provide for the collection of the taxes levied hereunder in not more than twenty annual installments, and it may fix the number of installments and the amount to be collected each year. Such installments shall be payable and shall be collected in each year at the same time that State and county taxes are due and payable. 

The statute requires that when such tax is levied the county clerk shall, at the expense of the district, prepare a list and schedule of all taxes levied in the form the statute prescribes. (Sec. 10823.) 

Under this statutory authority, it has been held that the county court may divide the apportionment against the county into installments, and such obligation may be enforced by action against the county by the drainage district for a general judgment.40 The fact that no assessment book was made up as required does not render the tax uncollectible or invalidate the assessment thereof.47 

Sec. 474. Additional Levies. 

Should the proceeds of the taxes first levied be insufficient to construct the improvements, the court shall make, certify and provide for the collection of such additional tax levies as are necessary to complete the improvements, but the aggregate of all such levies, exclusive of taxes levied for interest on bonds, should not exceed the total benefits assessed and confirmed (Sec. 10824). 45 949.

COUNTY COURTS Sec. 475. Taxes Levied Are a Lien. 

All taxes thus levied by the county court against lands and property in such drainage district, including maintenance taxes, together with all penalties for default in payment of the same, all costs in collecting the same, including a reasonable attorney's fee to be fixed by the court and taxed as costs in the action brought to enforce payment, shall, from date of the levying of the same by the county court until paid, constitute a lien, to which only the lien of the State for State, county, school and road taxes shall be paramount. 

Such lien shall exist against all of the lands assessed, and taxes for the retirement of the lien shall be collected in the same manner as State, county and school taxes upon real estate are collected. (Sec. 10828.) In a suit for the collection of such taxes, a defendant cannot attack the proceedings for the organization of the drainage district.48 Special assessments against land in a drainage district are not taxes in the general or legal acceptation of that term, but are assessments made for benefits received by the property from a public improvement.49 A personal judgment cannot be rendered for such assessments.50 Irregularities on the tax books do not invalidate the levy of such taxes.51

Sec. 476. Court May Issue Bonds of District. 

The statute authorizes the county to issue bonds for and on behalf of any such drainage district for the purpose of paying the costs of the completion of the improvement and the payment of the duly authorized expenses incident thereto. The aggregate par value of such bonds shall not exceed the taxes levied to pay the cost of the improvement and the expenses incident thereto, exclusive of the ten per cent for emergencies and the amount added to the tax levy to meet the interest on the bonds of the district. Such bonds shall be in denominations of one hundred dollars and multiples

Sec. 477. Additional Power of County Court Over Such District. 

The supervision of such districts, the government and control thereof, and the business incident to their operation are all placed in the hands of the county court, which has power in behalf of the district to construct the improvements for the district or to let contracts therefor (Sec. 10833), to appoint an engineer for the district, who may, with the approval of the court, appoint a consulting engineer (Sec. 10834), to levy a tax upon each tract of land within the district for the purpose of raising funds used in maintaining, preserving, restoring, repairing, strengthening, and replacing the drains, ditches, levees and other works of the district (Sec. 10844), and, for the purpose of maintaining, preserving, restoring, repairing, strengthening and replacing the drains, ditches and levees of such drainage districts, the county court is vested with authority for the continuous management and control thereof, and for that purpose all the drainage districts in a county may be administered as a unit if same is petitioned for by a majority of the landowners owning a majority of the land in each district in such county (Sec. 10843).

Sec. 478. Proceedings for Enlargement or Cleaning of Ditches. 

Proceedings for the enlargement, cleaning out and removal of obstructions from drainage ditches, may be had before the county court 557

COUNTY COURTS 

upon petition filed with the county clerk setting forth the necessity therefor. Notice must be published after the filing of such petition in some weekly newspaper published in the county at least three times, the last insertion to be before the day set for hearing. (Sec. 

10845.) After such notice is given, the county court is authorized to hear and summarily determine matters raised by the petition, and if the court finds that the owners of a majority in acreage of the district have signed the statement or have joined in the prayer of the statement by motion or otherwise, then the court shall find in favor of making the improvement and shall proceed with same (Sec. 10846).52
